name: Adoni-zedek
overview: Adoni-zedek was a male king who ruled over Jerusalem during the time of the Israelite conquest of the Promised Land. His role as King of Jerusalem situates him as a significant Canaanite ruler opposing the Israelites' advance. Scripture identifies him specifically in the book of Joshua, highlighting his political authority in the region.
namesAndTitles: The name Adoni-zedek means '[my] lord is righteousness,' reflecting a title of honor or divine association common in ancient Near Eastern royal names. Additionally, he is identified by the title 'King of Jerusalem,' which straightforwardly denotes his political position as the ruler of that city during the period described in Joshua 10:1.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Adoni-zedek beyond his identification as King of Jerusalem. There are no listed relatives or tribal affiliations associated with him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Adoni-zedek is significant in the biblical narrative as a chief opponent to Israel during the conquest of Canaan. His kingship over Jerusalem places him at the center of the resistance against God's people as they took possession of the land promised to them. His mention in Joshua 10:1 underscores the historical and theological conflict between the inhabitants of the land and the advancing Israelites under divine mandate.
